subject: Post-call: Pilot readiness & evaluation approach
messages:
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Jane Park <jane.park@carelink.com>, Tom Castillo <tom.castillo@carelink.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 07 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Post-call: Pilot readiness & evaluation approach

Hi Jane / Tom — thanks again for the demo today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we keep momentum: 

Recap from our call:
- Objective: Run a 4-week pilot to validate Redwood inference for patient triage summarization and routing in your care ops workflow.
- Primary constraint: PHI stays in your VPC; we discussed Private deployment options and KMS for key management.

Proposed success criteria (draft attached - pilot-success-criteria.xlsx):
1) Precision: >= 88% of triage summaries must map to the correct care pathway (clinician-verified sample)
2) Latency: 95th percentile inference latency <= 350ms for 256-token requests
3) Throughput: sustain 50 concurrent req/s for peak windows with <2% error rate
4) Safety/regulatory: zero accidental PHI exfiltration incidents; evidence through audit logs

Evaluation approach (we recommend two complementary tracks):
- Offline eval (week 0–1): Run your historical anonymized transcripts through Redwood to compute precision/recall vs labeled set. This gives a ground-truth baseline before live traffic.
- Online shadow (week 2–4): Shadow mode in production where Redwood receives live traffic copies (no user-facing changes) to validate model behavior and latency at scale.

Ownership & timeline (proposed):
- Week 0: Data & access prep (CareLink infra + S3 export) — Owner: Tom
- Week 1: Offline run and rubric grading — Owner: Marissa (CS) + CareLink SMEs
- Week 2–4: Shadow in prod + operational runbooks — Owner: Rishi (EngOps) + CareLink infra team

Immediate asks:
1) Confirm the success criteria above or propose edits (particularly the precision threshold).
2) Share a small anonymized sample (500–1,000 rows) we can run offline; S3 link preferred.
3) Confirm SSO/keys cadence and whether we should route through your KMS or Redwood-managed KMS for the pilot.

Attachments: pilot-success-criteria.xlsx (draft thresholds).

If this looks good I’ll send a short SOW draft and a calendar for the kickoff.

Thanks,
Neha Kapoor
Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0142

From: Jane Park <jane.park@carelink.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Castillo <tom.castillo@carelink.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 07 Dec 2026 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call: Pilot readiness & evaluation approach

Thanks, Neha — great summary. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Precision threshold: 88% is reasonable as a starting point, but can we add a secondary guardrail for false-positive severity? For example, for high-risk triage tags ("emergency," "escalate"), we want precision >= 95%.
- Data sample: We can provide 800 de-identified transcripts by EOD Wed (S3 link to follow).
- KMS / keys: Security prefers customer-managed KMS for the pilot. We'll share access details.

One question on evaluation methodology: will offline evaluation include the same normalization and pre-processing pipeline we run in prod? We want to ensure parity (tokenization, redaction steps).

On the DocuSign/SOW, please send the draft — procurement will need a short timeline and payment terms.

Appreciate the speedy follow-up.

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>

Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Tom Castillo <tom.castillo@carelink.com>
Date: Mon, 07 Dec 2026 13:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call: Pilot readiness & evaluation approach

Thanks Jane — good call on a high-risk guardrail. I pulled together a quick draft rubric (attached eval-rubric-v1.csv) that we plan to use for the offline run. Highlights: 

- Labeling protocol: CareLink SMEs label 1,000 samples; we hold out 20% for a validation fold.
- Metrics: precision@class, recall@class, overall F1, confusion matrix for top 5 classes.
- High-risk rule: any example labeled "escalate" must meet precision >= 95% else fail gate.
- Acceptance gates: 
  * Offline pass: overall F1 >= 0.75 AND per-class precision for critical tags >= thresholds
  * Shadow pass: system must meet latency & error-rate SLOs and show no systematic degradation vs offline labels

Operational notes: 
- Pre-processing parity: We’ll run an identical tokenization & redaction step as production; Tom, we’ll need the exact preprocessing script or a containerized binary.
- Monitoring: we’ll ship token-level latency traces, per-request metadata, and anonymized audit logs to your S3 bucket.

Next steps for CS/EngOps: 
- Marissa: run offline once we get the 800-sample set (timeline 48–72 hrs).
- Rishi: plan shadow rollout window and Canary rule (start at 5% of traffic, monitor 24h, increase by 2x/day).

2) Timeline (confirmed):

- Mon (Dec 14): Offline results & rubric scoring -> sync call (30 min) to review
- Tue (Dec 15)–Fri (Dec 18): Shadow rollout (5% -> 20% traffic based on canary rules)
- Mon (Dec 21): Final acceptance review and go/no-go decision

3) Owners: Tom = infra & data; Marissa = offline grading & results; Rishi = shadow rollout and monitoring; Neha = commercial & SOW.

4) Quick ask on redaction parity: please attach the preprocessing script or container to the S3 bucket. If you prefer, Rishi and Tom can do a short handoff call tomorrow.

If everything looks good I’ll:
- Upload the SOW to DocuSign and add Tom + Jane as signees
- Create the HubSpot task and set the kickoff calendar for Dec 9 10:00 AM PT

Best,
